page.title: How Do You Add Two Numbers in Python?
page.introduction: A simple Python program demonstrates several fundamental programming concepts together: receiving input, converting data types, assigning values to names, performing arithmetic, and displaying output.
page.definition: A Python program is a sequence of instructions that the Python interpreter executes to perform a task. In this example, the program accepts two numbers, calculates their sum, and displays the result.

explanation.content: A complete learning example should connect the concept, its important characteristics, a visual representation, and an executable example.

The following program demonstrates a simple input-processing-output flow. The user enters two values, Python converts those values from text into integers, performs addition, and finally displays the calculated result.
The program can be understood as four simple stages: Input → Conversion → Calculation → Output.

characteristics.title: Input
characteristics.description: The program receives two values from the user through the input() function.

characteristics.title: Type Conversion
characteristics.description: The int() function converts the text returned by input() into integer values.

characteristics.title: Calculation
characteristics.description: The + operator performs arithmetic addition on the two integer values.

characteristics.title: Assignment
characteristics.description: The calculated result is assigned to the name sum.

characteristics.title: Output
characteristics.description: The print() function displays the final result to the terminal.

characteristics.title: Sequential Execution
characteristics.description: Python executes the statements in the program sequentially from top to bottom.

visual.introduction: The program follows a simple data-flow model in which user input moves through conversion and calculation before becoming the final output.

rows.title: User Input
rows.description: Two numbers entered by the user

explanation.content: The user first provides two values. Each value is passed through int() so Python can treat it as an integer.
The two integers are then added together. The resulting value is stored in sum and displayed using print().

example.introduction: Let's implement the complete flow using Python. The program accepts two integers from the user and prints their sum.
example.description: This example demonstrates input, integer conversion, assignment, arithmetic addition, and output in a single small Python program.

output.label: Terminal Output
output.value:
Enter first number: 10
Enter second number: 20
Sum = 30

explanation.content: The first line calls input() to receive the first value. Because input() returns text, int() converts that text into an integer and the result is assigned to num1.
The second line performs the same operation for the second value and stores it in num2.
The expression num1 + num2 performs integer addition and assigns the resulting value to sum.
Finally, print("Sum =", sum) sends the calculated result to the terminal.

page.takeaway: The complete example connects the definition, characteristics, visual flow, and executable code into one learning model: receive input, convert it to integers, calculate the sum, and display the result.
